extracted.intended_audience: transit agencies, project sponsors, planners, stakeholders and members of the public interested in FTA New Starts/Small Starts programs
extracted.subtask_description: A Federal Transit Administration notice informing the public about the status of the New Starts and Small Starts policy guidance (no significant changes proposed), the statutory requirement to publish guidance periodically, and where to find the current review process and related rulemaking activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory publication requirement (49 U.S.C. 5309(d)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 5309(d)(6) of Title 49, U.S. Code, requires the Federal Transit Administration (FTA) to publish policy guidance on the New and Small Starts capital project review and evaluation process and criteria each time significant changes are made, but not less frequently than once every two years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FTA must publish policy guidance on the New and Small Starts review and evaluation process and criteria upon significant changes and at least biennially. This is a statutory obligation that drives the timing of notices like this one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of no significant changes to guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: This notice informs the public that no significant changes are proposed to the existing guidance on the New Starts and Small Starts programs and that FTA intends to continue use of existing guidance at this time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice serves to satisfy the publication requirement by announcing continuation of the current guidance. It references that FTA last published Guidance on New and Small Starts Policies and Procedures in September 2009 and points readers to FTA's website for information describing the current review process (http://www.fta.dot.gov/​planning/​planning_​environment_​5221.html).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction from ANPRM on project justification criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: This notification should not be confused with the Advanced Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (ANPRM) published by FTA in June 2010, which sought public comment on the New Starts and Small Starts project justification criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information gathered from the ANPRM is being used to inform FTA's broader effort to amend the regulations that govern the New Starts and Small Starts programs. The current notice does not itself propose regulatory changes to those criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and legal-status of FederalRegister.gov XML rendition
rubrics_metrics.description: The FederalRegister.gov page displays a prototype XML rendition of the daily Federal Register and is not an official legal edition; each document includes a link to the corresponding official PDF on govinfo.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Until the Administrative Committee of the Federal Register (ACFR) issues a regulation granting official status, the XML rendition on FederalRegister.gov does not provide legal notice to the public or judicial notice to the courts. Users relying on the material for legal research should verify against the official print or govinfo.gov PDF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural metadata and contact/ effective date information
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice provides procedural information including the effective date (August 16, 2011) and contact points for programmatic and legal questions (Elizabeth Day, Office of Planning and Environment; Christopher Van Wyk, Office of Chief Counsel).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices should include effective dates and contact information so stakeholders can follow up with program or legal questions; office hours and telephone numbers are provided for public inquiries.
